description:
🚀 Goal: Design a user-friendly dashboard tracking space hazards (radiation, bone loss, immune shifts) for astronaut health. 
💡 Looking for: • UI & UX Designer: High-tech dashboard & Pitch Video. • Front-End Dev: Interactive web prototype. • Space & Health Tech enthusiasts! 📩 Join our crew and let’s build something awesome together! 🚀✨
summary:
Asterism is a visual health self-check tool for astronauts on long-duration missions. On a trip to Mars, a message to Earth and back takes up to 44 minutes, so crews cannot rely on a doctor in real time. They must measure, understand, and act on their own health.

Each day, an astronaut spends about two minutes logging blood pressure, heart rate, blood glucose, body temperature, SpO2, sleep, and mood by keyboard, tap, or camera. Asterism then draws the body as a constellation: each star is a body system, labelled Nominal, Watch, or Act, based on how readings compare with the astronaut's pre-flight baseline. Tapping a star explains what the reading means, what to do now, and when to contact the flight surgeon.

Asterism maps every indicator to the five spaceflight hazards identified by NASA's Human Research Program and explains each reading in that context. It works offline, adapts to different mission environments, and uses reminders and streaks to keep the routine going. The same approach can help people far from medical care on Earth.
details:
Project Details: Asterism – Crew Health Self-Check Dashboard

1. What does it do or how does it work? Asterism is an interactive, web-based daily health self-check prototype designed for astronauts on long-duration space missions (such as a Mars transit). Accessible via a live public interface (asterism-btas.netlify.app), it lets crew members log vital health indicators—including blood pressure, heart rate, blood glucose, body temperature, SpO2, sleep duration, and mood—in about two minutes each day. Instead of relying on population averages, Asterism compares each reading against the astronaut's pre-flight baseline using a visual "body constellation" map where each star represents a body system. Readings are dynamically evaluated into three clear statuses (Nominal, Watch, Act) based on standard clinical thresholds and trend tracking (e.g., three consecutive check-ins outside the baseline). Tapping a system star instantly provides actionable "Do Now" steps and flight surgeon contact guidelines.

2. What benefits does it have?

  • Autonomous Decision Support: Bridges the communication gap during deep-space exploration where round-trip communication delays with Earth can reach up to 44 minutes, empowering crews to assess health states locally without real-time physician oversight.
  • Contextual Hazard Mapping: Links every monitored indicator directly to NASA’s Human Research Program (HRP) five spaceflight hazards (RIDGE: Radiation, Isolation, Distance, Gravity, Environment), helping crews understand why physiological shifts happen.
  • Offline-First Resilience: Engineered to function reliably in isolated habitats without continuous internet connectivity.

3. What is the intended impact of the project? Asterism aims to safeguard astronaut health and performance on multi-month or multi-year deep-space missions by transforming complex medical data into intuitive, actionable daily routines. By utilizing streaks, gamified XP, and routine reminders, it sustains crew engagement and mitigates cognitive fatigue. Furthermore, its decentralized, self-monitoring framework holds profound terrestrial utility, offering accessible telehealth decision support for remote populations, polar research stations, and isolated communities far from medical infrastructure on Earth.

4. What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use to develop your project?

  • Frontend Development: HTML5, CSS3, and Vanilla JavaScript structured into a single-file, lightweight architecture ensuring instant local execution and offline compatibility.
  • UI/UX & Typography: Responsive design built with custom CSS variables, featuring interactive SVG body-mapping and trend charts, styled with Google Fonts (Space Grotesk, Inter, JetBrains Mono).
  • Deployment & Hosting: Hosted publicly via Netlify ([https://asterism-btas.netlify.app](https://asterism-btas.netlify.app)) for seamless global accessibility.
  • Reference Frameworks: Grounded in NASA HRP research, the five RIDGE spaceflight hazards, and standard clinical reference parameters.

5. How is your project creative? Asterism reimagines traditional, clinical medical charts through a unique "constellation of the body" metaphor. By translating abstract biomedical numbers into an interactive star map of organ systems, it lowers cognitive load for fatigued astronauts. Moreover, its dual-layer alert system combines personal baseline deviations with multi-day trend analysis (detecting gradual drifts rather than single-point anomalies). It seamlessly maps them to NASA's spaceflight hazards.

6. What factors did your team consider?

  • Scientific Validity & Realism: Avoided unverified assumptions by grounding threshold models in standard clinical reference ranges and synthetic 14-day crew datasets, ensuring strict alignment with real spaceflight human research principles.
  • Usability under Stress: Designed an ultra-fast, 2-minute daily check-in flow with clear visual color-coding (Nominal, Watch, Act) tailored for high-workload aerospace environments.
  • Privacy & Autonomy: Prioritized localized data storage and personal baseline tracking, recognizing that spacefarers require private, trustworthy tools for routine self-assessments before downlinking summaries to flight surgeons.
